summary:
CADET-NAUTS is a Roblox-based educational adventure created for the NASA Space Apps Challenge: Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer. Our game helps children ages 7–12 learn what it takes to survive on a lunar mission by turning real astronaut decisions into interactive gameplay. 

Players go on a 14-day Moon mission, manage resources like oxygen, water, and power, and solve problems inspired by real space challenges such as radiation events, equipment failures, and habitat maintenance. Days 1–7 are introduced through a cinematic story, and Days 8–14 are playable. 

Our goal is to make space science fun, accessible, and exciting by using real NASA resources in a platform children already know and love: Roblox.

Please note that Roblox is very strict with age restrictions hence it is a process to get our game checked and verified on that end - it is delays from their end to get this game accessible to the target age range (and we could not receieve approval in the 2 days we had to create this)
details:
CADET-NAUTS is an educational Roblox game designed for children ages 7–12. It was created for the NASA Space Apps Challenge under the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge. The purpose of the project is to help younger learners understand how astronauts survive and make decisions in space through interactive storytelling and gameplay.

In the game, players become junior astronauts on a 14-day Moon mission. The first 7 days are presented as a cinematic introduction that introduces the crew, the mission, the spacecraft, and the lunar base systems. The remaining 7 days are interactive, allowing players to complete tasks, respond to emergencies, and manage limited resources such as oxygen, water, and electricity. Each decision comes with a cost, teaching players that survival in space depends on careful choices and trade-offs.

The gameplay is built around age-appropriate minigames and challenges. These include repairing systems, restoring water supply, managing greenhouse problems, responding to power loss, and dealing with radiation-related events. We simplified complex engineering ideas into clear, engaging mechanics so children can learn through play rather than memorization.

Our project is creative because it combines real NASA-inspired science, cinematic storytelling, and playful Roblox gameplay in a format that is highly accessible to young users. We chose Roblox because it is a platform already familiar to millions of children worldwide, which makes our educational experience easier to access and more likely to reach a large audience.

To develop the project, we used game design planning, storyboarding, visual asset creation, character design, UI mockups, and NASA data research. Our visual direction focused on child-friendly 3D cartoon characters, simple interfaces, and mission-based progression that supports curiosity, exploration, and learning.

The intended impact of CADET-NAUTS is to make space education more interactive, memorable, and accessible while inspiring children to become interested in science, engineering, and exploration.
